newsitem.title: USA: Closing arguments set in Time Warner suit.
newsitem.headline: Closing arguments set in Time Warner suit.

text.p: A federal judge set closing arguments for Wednesday in Time Warner's suit against New York City aimed at stopping it from airing Rupert Murdoch's Fox News Network or Bloomberg Television News on city-run cable channels.
The hearing is scheduled to begin at 9:30 EST before U.S. District Judge Denise Cote in Manhattan federal court.
Cote said in a hearing Tuesday that she did not expect to rule on Wednesday but did plan to issue a decision quickly.

Cote previously granted Time Warner's request for a temporary order halting efforts by New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani to run the Fox 24-hour news channel. She has been hearing arguments during a hearing that began Monday over Time Warner's request for a permanent bar.

The dispute centres on the role of the city's five stations, known as Crosswalks. Giuliani decided to place the new Fox channel on one of the of the Crosswalks channels after Time Warner rejected it. He also plans to run Bloomberg Television News, which also is not aired by Time Warner.

Time Warner, which serves 1.1 million customers in New York, sued the city alleging that Giuliani was acting on behalf of Murdoch's News Corp. Ltd., which owns the New York Post and WNYW-TV. It said in its suit that the city was acting as Murdoch's "latest political puppet."
It alleged that the plan violated its franchise agreement with the city. Time Warner argued that the agreement provides that the city-run channels be used for non-commercial purposes.

Time Warner also alleged that the Federal Cable Act prohibits governmental stations from being used for commercial use. In addition, it alleged that the city's plan violates Time Warner's free speech rights because it is infringing on its editorial discretion by trying to force it to carry the two news channels.
